title: Lint for fixed colors paired with theme colors
summary: Mostly a developer check: a new lint rule flags places where text has a fixed color (like white) on a background that changes with the theme, or the reverse. Fixing the places it found changes one small thing you can see: in **Dark** mode, the arrow on an opened reference in the References view is now dark instead of white. A color change at the bottom of the translation picker should have no visible effect, and everything else should look exactly as before.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link above in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac.

setup.title: Know how to switch themes
setup.body: Most tests are done twice, once in the light theme and once in the dark one. To switch, open **Settings**, go to **Theme & text**, and pick **Light** or **Dark**. Signing in isn't needed.

sections.title: Custom translations link in the translation picker
sections.intro: The bottom area of the translation picker had its default text color changed from a bright red-orange to the app's standard orange. Everything in that area sets its own color, so nothing there should look different.

tests.title: The Custom translations row looks the same as before in the light theme
steps: Click the translation name at the top of the reader (for example **BSB**) to open the translation picker.
Scroll to the very bottom of the list.
Look at the **Custom translations** row and its **+** icon.
expected: The **Custom translations** text and its **+** icon use the same normal text color as the rest of the picker (dark in the light theme), not orange.
The text is easy to read against the background.

tests.title: The Custom translations row looks the same as before in the dark theme
steps: Open the translation picker again and scroll to the bottom.
expected: The **Custom translations** text and its **+** icon use the normal light text color of the dark theme and are easy to read.

tests.title: The Custom translations area still opens and looks right
steps: Click **Custom translations** at the bottom of the translation picker.
expected: The first click opens the custom translations area: an **Enter URL** box and an orange **Import** button with readable text, and the **+** icon changes to a **−**.
The second click closes it again.

sections.title: Opened reference arrow in the References view
sections.intro: When you open one reference in the References list, its round arrow button turns orange. In the dark theme, the arrow on it is now dark instead of white.

setup.title: Open the References view
setup.body: Open **John 3** and open **Discover**. Pick the **References** chip at the top. If the app offers to download reference data, accept it and wait until the list appears. If you don't see a **References** chip, open **Settings**, then **Extensions**, install **References**, and try again.

tests.title: The opened reference's arrow shows white on orange in the light theme
steps: In the References list, click the round arrow button at the right of any reference to show its text.
expected: The reference opens and shows its verse text.
The arrow button is a solid orange circle with a **white** arrow pointing up, the same as before this change.

tests.title: The opened reference's arrow is clearly visible in the dark theme
tests.why: This is the main visible change. In the dark theme the app's text-on-orange color is dark, so the arrow now follows it. Before this change it was always white.
tests.before: Switch the theme to **Dark** and go back to the References list.
steps: Open a reference with its round arrow button, as in the previous test.
expected: The arrow button is a solid orange circle with a **dark (near-black)** arrow pointing up.
The arrow is easy to see against the orange.

tests.title: Closing a reference returns the arrow to normal
steps: Click the orange arrow button on the opened reference.
expected: The verse text hides again and the arrow button goes back to its plain, non-orange look, pointing down.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed
sections.intro: These buttons were checked by the new rule and deliberately left with white text.

tests.title: The Install button on an extension's page keeps white text in both themes
steps: Click an extension that isn't installed yet to open its page.
Look at the **Install** button in the **Light** theme.
Switch to the **Dark** theme and look at the **Install** button again.
expected: In both themes, the **Install** button is a darker orange with **white** text that's easy to read.
Don't press **Install** unless you want the extension; this test is only about how the button looks.

tests.title: The rest of the app looks the same in both themes
steps: In the **Light** theme, browse a chapter, open the translation picker, open **Settings**, and open **Discover**.
Switch to the **Dark** theme and do the same.
expected: Buttons, tabs, and highlights look the same as on the live site. Nothing has text that's hard to read or a color that looks out of place.

notCovered: The new lint rule itself and its automated tests. They only run for developers and in CI.
The unread-message count bubble in the chat list now uses the theme's text-on-orange color (dark in the dark theme). Reaching it needs a chat with unread messages, which is hard to set up by hand.
The "Navigating to …" notice in the Twitch extension now uses the theme's secondary text color instead of white. Reaching it needs a live Twitch setup.
A style change for the mobile split-panel warning button. No screen in the app currently uses that style.
The "Allow" button in the extension permission window keeps white text, like the **Install** button tested above. That window only appears for some extensions.
